text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.

- Russia may close two weather observation stations in Saint Peterburg and Murmansk whose information is extremely imoprtant for Finnish meteorologists to detect the route of radioactive clouds in case of nuclear accidents.
- European Union to investigate European airlines' cooperation agreements, including Finnair's arrangements with American Delta Arlines.
- Finnish researcher Heikki Karppinen has sought a patent for a food additive product based on plant sterol which he says would lower cholestrol levels in the blood.

- Foreign funds and investment banks last week bought Finnish markka for billions of marks, but only the first round of the game against the markka has been played, London sources say. City dealers believe markka gains have been purely speculative.
- Publishing house Kauppakaari, which specialises in legal publications, seeks growth by acquisitions in Estonia and Sweden.
- Media advertising rose only a few percent last year to 4.7 billion markka, failing expectations of stronger growth.
- Finnish state railways (VR) to decide in September on whether to order 23 Italian Fiat Ferrovaria Pendolino trains for 1.8 billion markka. VR has been testing two prototypes. @
- State asset management company Arsenal to come under strict supervision of a special parliamentary committee to be set up by the ministry of finance.
- President Ahtisaari to visit South Africa in May at the invitation of President Nelson Mandela.
- Central Union of Agricultural producers questions Finnish army's purchases of mostly imported vegetables from Hungary and Poland.
